story_of_day.headline: Trump lands in China for a three-way summit with Xi and Putin
story_of_day.story: Xi greeted Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen, returning the favour from his Washington visit in September. On Thursday Trump, Xi and Putin sit down together at the APEC summit, a first of its kind. Analysts expect few concrete results on trade or tech. Putin arrives after Ukraine partly collapsed the Kerch bridge, and says Europe is in 'humiliating decline'.
story_of_day.so_what: The signal matters more than any deal: Moscow and Beijing get to be seen as equals with Washington while Europe is left out. Watch for any hint of a Ukraine settlement being discussed without Kyiv or Brussels.

last_time.text: Then China was threatening retaliation over new US chip limits; now the leaders have arrived and the mood is polite but low on expectations.

cards.headline: Another ship hit in Hormuz as Iran targets supertankers
cards.story: An ADNOC Logistics vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, and one crew member is still missing. Small tankers carried a wartime-high 2 million barrels a day out of the Strait in October, while supertankers are being avoided as incidents with mines and unknown projectiles hit a wartime peak. Saudi-led forces also struck 60 Houthi sites as the Houthis push toward Aden.
cards.so_what: Shipping is adapting around the danger, not escaping it. Yemen is a second front that could threaten Red Sea routes too.

last_time.text: Then Iran had hit Bahrain and a gas tanker burned; now a state oil company's ship has been hit and Yemen is flaring.

cards.money_angle: Brent is $90.30, down from $93.07 last run. The market is still looking past the attacks.

cards.headline: The Iran war reaches British bills: inflation 3.6%, energy up 26% in January
cards.story: UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October as petrol prices climbed and diesel hit a record high. Regulated household energy bills are forecast to jump 26% to about £2,166 a year from January, an extra £443.
cards.so_what: This is how a far-off shipping war becomes a cost-of-living story. It limits how far the Bank of England can cut and adds pressure on the government.

cards.headline: ICJ rules Thursday on Myanmar's genocide against the Rohingya
cards.story: The International Court of Justice will rule on The Gambia's case against Myanmar. The court has never before found a state responsible for genocide. Fears are growing that the US could sanction ICJ judges, including Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay, if the ruling goes against Myanmar.
cards.so_what: Bangladesh hosts around a million Rohingya refugees, so a ruling would put pressure on Dhaka's repatriation talks. It could also set a precedent for the court's case on Israel and Gaza.

cards.headline: Bangladesh braces for a Jamaat march as Awami League unrest continues
cards.story: Police detained 71 Awami League activists in Dhaka in 24 hours and recovered more than 2kg of gunpowder. A petrol bomb killed an activist in Hasina's home district, and security forces are deployed in Gopalganj ahead of an Awami League programme. Jamaat plans a rally and march in Dhaka on 21 November over the political violence. A lawyer also served notice demanding the government bring Hasina back within 15 days.
cards.so_what: Violence from several sides raises the odds of clashes on the 21st. Cyclone Akvan is also approaching, adding strain on the state.

last_time.text: Then Awami League supporters had torched a police station; now police are cracking down and Jamaat is calling its own march.

watch.title: 21 November in Dhaka
watch.text: Jamaat's march and the aftermath of Thursday's trilateral summit and ICJ ruling.
